newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Trgovacka Banka says appoints new board. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Croatian Trgovacka Banka says appoints new board. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]

text.p: Croatian private bank Trgovacka Banka said on Thursday it had appointed a new board directors this week after the resignations of the president and another board member.
"Boris Ninic was named president on Monday," spokesman Tomislav Vuic told Reuters. Ninic will move from the post of legal department head at the bank.
He will replace Damir Odak, who is leaving due to differences over the method of raising new capital for the bank, Vuic confirmed.
Sladjana Jagar, formerly the head of interior control, becomes a new director instead of Sanja Martinko while Boris Centner and Branko Kondic remain on the board.
Trgovacka will propose to its annual meeting on June 19 to increase equity by 2.6 million kuna from last year's profits to 71.6 million.
Half of its 27.8 million 1996 net was allotted to dividen payments of 220 kuna per share. The bank plans to retain 9.5 million.

Odak, who controlled almost 10 percent of Trgovacka and was one of the biggest single shareholders, was advocating a larger new share issue to boost the bank's resources and improve its market position.
Trgovacka was among the first of a handful of smaller Croatian banks to get a credit line for propping up private enterprises from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in 1996.

Vuic said Odak had recently sold his stake to a private investor. Metroholding, a private company which owns another bank -- Partner Banka, also acquired around six percent in Trgovacka (corrects the buyer of Odak's stake).
However no plans have been announced yet to merge the two in the face of increasing competition in Croatia's overcrowded banking sector.
